key_insight: A general-purpose language model can directly write small neural-network weights that rank material candidates without property labels and improve early-stage discovery.
engineering_relevance: These label-free predictors can initialize Bayesian optimization and screen generated crystals when measurements are scarce.
method: Provide the language model with the task, input names, and a zero-initialized network with 16 hidden units.
Have it fill in every network weight directly as text.
Use the resulting predictor for ranking, Bayesian prior means, or generator screening.
evidence_signal: At five labels, the weight-written Gaussian-process prior increased ranking correlations from 0.35 to 0.69 on experimental alloys and from 0.15 to 0.95 on crystals; Bayesian optimization regret fell significantly on 4 of 5 experimental tasks.
watch_item: Benefits are limited to the first tens of labels and targets not already well ranked by simple rules or subsystem extrapolation.
